q: 1. The safety of the structure can be disturbed by ...........
options: lowering or rising of water table
excavations in the immediate vicinity of the structure
mining or tunneling operations in the neighborhood
explain: Structural stability depends on the ground conditions; changes in water pressure, nearby soil removal (excavation), or underground voids (mining) can all cause settlement or failure.

q: 2. The foundation in a building is provided to
options: distribute the load over a large area
increase overall stability of the structure
transmit load to the bearing surface (sub soil) at a uniform rate
explain: Foundations serve multiple structural purposes: spreading concentrated loads to prevent soil failure, ensuring stability against sliding or overturning, and ensuring uniform pressure on the subsoil.

q: 3. The minimum depth of foundation below the ground level in any soil is .........
explain: In general practice and to avoid frost action or surface disturbances, the minimum recommended depth for any foundation is 80 cm to 90 cm.

q: 4. The approximate bearing capacity of a sound rock without any defects may be taken as .........
explain: Hard, sound rocks like granite or limestone have very high bearing capacities, typically ranging from 300 to 350 t/m².

q: 5. When two or more footing are connected by a beam, is called
explain: A strap footing (or cantilever footing) consists of two individual footings connected by a structural 'strap' beam. This is often used when one footing is placed against a property line.

q: 6. If the load coming on to a pile is transferred to a suitable bearing stratum at its bottom end, then it is called .........
explain: An end-bearing pile transfers the structural load directly through its tip to a hard, incompressible layer of rock or dense gravel.

q: 7. If the load coming on to a pile is resisted by friction developed between the surface area of the pile and the surrounding material, then it is called .........
explain: Friction piles derive their carrying capacity from the skin friction (adhesion) between the pile surface and the surrounding soil.

q: 8. Bearing capacity of soils cannot be improved by
explain: Watering the surface usually softens the soil and increases pore water pressure, which actually reduces the shear strength and bearing capacity rather than improving it.

q: 9. The maximum permissible differential settlement in the case of foundations on clayey soils is generally about ...........
explain: Clayey soils allow for a higher differential settlement (40 mm) because the settlement process is slower and more uniform over time compared to sand.

q: 10. The bearing capacity of water logged soil, may be improved by
explain: For waterlogged soil, the most effective first step is drainage. Removing excess water reduces pore pressure and increases the effective stress (and thus strength) of the soil grains.

q: 11. The maximum permissible total settlement in the case of raft foundations sandy soils is generally about ...........
explain: For rafts on sand, the allowable total settlement is usually limited to 65 mm (standard range 40–65 mm) to ensure stability.

q: 12. The safe bearing capacity under dynamic loads such as machine foundations is taken to be...
options: more than that for static loads
same as that for static loads
less than that for static loads
depends on the weight of machine
explain: Dynamic/vibratory loads can cause soil liquefaction or additional settlement, so the allowable bearing capacity is reduced (often by 25-50%) compared to static loads.

q: 13. The tilt in the well foundations should not exceed .........
explain: During the sinking of caissons/wells, the vertical alignment (tilt) is strictly monitored and should not deviate more than 1 in 200.

q: 14. The maximum total settlement for raft foundation on clayey soils is usually limited to
explain: For clayey soils, raft foundations are generally designed to limit total settlement to 65-100 mm.

q: 15. The process of finding out the soil strata below ground level is known as
explain: Subsoil exploration involves boring and sampling to determine the engineering properties and layers of the soil before construction.

q: 16. The highest point on the extrados of the arch is known as ..........
explain: The crown is the highest part or apex of the arch's exterior curve.

q: 17. Generally for a column in a workshop using Gantry cranes, the foundation to be used should be
explain: Grillage foundations are used for heavy isolated column loads to spread the pressure over a larger area of soil.

q: 18. Ventilation means ..........
options: replacing the impure air in the building by fresh air from outside
explain: The fundamental purpose of ventilation is the continuous supply of fresh outdoor air and the removal of contaminated indoor air.

q: 19. Which of the following has the highest bearing capacity?
explain: Hard igneous rocks like granite or basalt have extremely high bearing capacities, often exceeding 3000 kN/m2.

q: 20. Black cotton soil is often termed as treacherous soil. The reason being ..........
explain: Black cotton soil contains montmorillonite clay which expands and contracts violently with moisture changes, causing foundation failure.

q: 21. The black cotton soil is unsuitable for foundations because
options: it is difficult to excavate it
explain: Black cotton soil has a low bearing capacity and is highly susceptible to volumetric changes (swelling and shrinking) due to moisture variations.

q: 22. The instrument generally used to measure the depth of foundation is ..........
explain: Boning rods are used in sets (usually three) to check levels and maintain a uniform depth or gradient in foundation trenches.

q: 23. The lower part of a structure which transmits the load to the soil is known as ..........
explain: The foundation is the lowest part of a building that receives the total load and distributes it safely over a large area of soil.

q: 24. The minimum load which causes the failure of a foundation is called ............ of the soil.
explain: Ultimate bearing strength is the maximum gross pressure at the base of the foundation at which the soil fails in shear.

q: 25. The safe bearing capacity of a soil is given by ..........
options: ultimate bearing strength / factor of safety
nominal strength x factor of safety
ultimate bearing strength x factor of safety
explain: Safe bearing capacity is calculated by dividing the ultimate bearing capacity by a Factor of Safety (usually 2 to 3).

q: 26. For the buildings on clayey soils, the minimum depth of foundation is ..........
explain: In clayey soils, foundations must be deeper to avoid the zone of seasonal moisture variation; typically 0.9m to 1.6m is required.

q: 27. The weight of the furniture stored in a building is termed as ..........
explain: Live loads (or imposed loads) include the weight of movable objects like furniture, occupants, and stored goods that are not a permanent part of the structure.

q: 28. The ability of sub-soil to support the load of the structure without yielding is known as ..........
explain: Bearing capacity (or value/power) refers to the soil's resistance to compression and shear failure under structural loads.

q: 29. The maximum bearing capacity of soil is that of ..........
explain: Igneous and hard rocks have the highest safe bearing capacity, often exceeding 3000-4000 kN/m².

q: 30. In order to protect the beam against corrosion, a minimum cover of ........ is kept on the outer sides of the external beams as well as above the upper flange of the top tier.
explain: In grillage foundations, steel beams are encased in concrete with at least 100 mm cover to protect against moisture and corrosion.

q: 31. Which of the following foundation is used for weaker soil?
explain: While all spread footings help, raft foundations are specifically designed to handle the most challenging weak soil conditions.

q: 32. The piles which do not support the load by themselves, but act as a medium to transmit the load from the foundation to the resisting sub-stratum, are known as ..........
explain: End-bearing piles act like columns, transmitting the load through their tips directly to a hard-resisting layer.

q: 33. The piles which are driven in the type of soil whose strength does not increase with depth or where the rate of increase in strength with depth is very slow, are known as ..........
explain: Friction piles derive their carrying capacity from the skin friction between the pile surface and the surrounding soil along the entire length of the pile.

q: 34. Fender piles are ..........
options: used to function as retaining walls
used to protect concrete deck or other water front structures from the abrasion or impact
driven at an inclination to resist large horizontal inclined forces
driven in granular soil with the aim of increasing the bearing capacity of the soil
explain: Fender piles are provided in waterfront structures to absorb the impact of berthing ships and protect the main structure from damage.

q: 35. Cast-in-situ piles is ..........
options: are cast in position inside the ground
need not be reinforced in ordinary cases
are not subjected to handling or driving stresses
explain: Since they are formed in the ground, cast-in-situ piles avoid the stresses of transport and driving, allowing for more flexible design.

options: cannot withstand large impact stress developed during hand driving
explain: H-piles (steel I-beams) are actually easy to store, handle, and can withstand extremely high driving stresses, making all the provided negative statements false.

q: 37. A steel pile which function more efficiently in soft clay or loose sand, is ..........
explain: The large helical blades of a screw pile provide significant uplift and bearing resistance in soft or loose soils.

q: 38. Sheet piles are made of ..........
explain: Sheet piles can be made of timber for light work, reinforced concrete for permanent structures, or steel for high-strength temporary or permanent shoring.

q: 39. When the pile is required to penetrate beds of hard soil or soft rock to reach its required depth, the best method of driving the pile is by ..........
explain: Boring (pre-drilling) removes the hard material that a standard hammer cannot penetrate, allowing the pile to reach the design depth.

q: 40. Pile foundation are provided ..........
explain: Piles are deep foundations used when surface soil is weak, water-logged, or compressible, to transfer loads to deeper, firmer strata.

q: 41. A type of foundation in which a cantilever beam is used for joining the two footings is ..........
explain: A strap footing connects two individual footings with a rigid beam (strap), often used when one footing is on a property line.

q: 42. The depth of excavation for foundation is usually checked with a ..........
explain: Boning rods are T-shaped wooden rods used in sets to maintain or check the correct levels and depths of trenches.

q: 43. Different types of pitched roofs are ...........
explain: Pitched roofs are categorized by their shape and slope; Gable roofs have two sloping sides meeting at a ridge, while Mansard roofs have four sides with two different slopes on each side.
